The test image shows soybean stems/petioles with distinct reddish-brown to dark purple longitudinal discoloration. Key features:
- Affected part: petioles/stems
- Elongated brownish-purple streaking along the stem/petiole
- Green pods visible nearby (still developing)
- No white mold, no powdery coating, no obvious pycnidia rows

Top candidates: **Cercospora** (reddish-purple lesions on petioles/stems) or **Anthracnose** (brown spots on stems/petioles). Let me view the Anthracnose reference to compare.

The Anthracnose reference shows distinct dark gray/black acervuli spots on tan/dry pods — very different from the test image.

The test image shows:
- **Green, living petiole** with **reddish-purple to dark brown longitudinal discoloration**
- No dark acervuli spots, no dry/dead tissue
- The pattern is a continuous purple-brown streak along the petiole

This matches **Cercospora** precisely: "reddish-purple lesions on petioles, stems, and pods" + "small dark spots along major leaf veins and petioles" — the purple-bronze discoloration caused by cercosporin toxin on living green tissue.

The tissue is still green and living (ruling out Anthracnose which shows dry, dead tissue with black acervuli). No white mold, no pycnidia rows, no angular leaf spots were observed."}
